claim_decisions.statement: Source dated 2026-05-05 reports: IMF says adaptation progress is constrained by limited institutional capacity, fragmented interagency coordination, and weak climate-risk integration in fiscal and infrastructure planning; it also identifies political fragmentation and administrative capacity as fragility drivers.
claim_decisions.locator: Physical PDF p.19, paragraph 28; physical PDF pp.39–40, Annex I fragility/coordination discussion.
claim_decisions.uncertainty: IMF institutional synthesis; political fragmentation and coordination constraints are not evidence of armed conflict or quantified state-level climate losses.

gaps: NDC water-service percentages have different or ambiguous denominators; they must not be used as a direct island inequality ratio.
No new complete climate–violence chain is inferred from capacity constraints or the IMF's use of fragility terminology.

executive_assessment.text: The NDC adds Yap/western Chuuk water-risk and tenure/governance detail, while the 2010 report supplies explicitly historical Pohnpei outer-atoll, Chuuk and Yap examples.
Adaptation financing, technical skills and coordination constrain implementation; these institutional findings are not a claim that climate causes violence.
